paper_metadata.title: Unveiling the Re effect in Ni-based single crystal superalloys

evidence.quote: Single crystal Ni-based superalloys have long been an essential material for gas turbines in aero engines and power plants due to their outstanding high temperature creep, fatigue and oxidation resistance.

For investigating the effect of Re on the creep response, the single crystal superalloy ERBO/1 is used 32. As shown in Table 1 in the Methods section, ERBO/1 contains 3 wt% (0.9 at%) Re, and is very close in composition to the commercial alloy CMSX-4.

mechanisms.material_state: crept at 750 °C and 800 MPa, interrupted at 5% strain

evidence.quote: the increase of Re in the PD must originate from solutes transported from the γ matrix into γ′, likely via pipe diffusion11,41–44.

conflicts.description: Re clustering in gamma phase has been reported by some studies and discounted by others; the present work does not resolve clustering directly.

evidence.quote: Blavette et al. 28,29 found evidence for small Re clusters in γ using a one-dimensional atom probe. On the other hand, more recent observations based on atom probe tomography (APT) show no Re clustering, discounting as such the possible role of Re clustering in improving the creep properties of Ni-based superalloys 23,30,31.
